principles: Respect the raw-output-never-surfaced security invariant: surface only token-count numbers from the provider runners, never raw transcript or stderr.
Reuse the existing adapter+assemble layer (buildProviderRecord already supports openai/gemini); add only the missing seam, do not duplicate normalization.
Keep the claude path and the ledger-OFF path byte-identical; every ledger call is fail-open.
Mirror existing precedent (extractCodexModel for extraction, the claude seam for wiring) to minimize novelty on a security-sensitive path.
drivers: Security invariant: a provider transcript must never leak into the surfaced result or into gate evidence.
No regression to the claude-code real-leaf path or the ledger-OFF byte-identical behavior.
usage-ledger zero-cross-module-import discipline: providers/ must not import usage-ledger.

options.name: A: runner extracts token-count-only usage; neutral reportedUsage; canonical per-provider final at the seam
pros: Surfaces only non-sensitive token numbers, so the raw-never-surfaced invariant holds
No usage-ledger import into providers/ (reportedUsage is a neutral Record)
Reuses buildProviderRecord openai/gemini support; minimal new code
Mirrors extractCodexModel and the existing claude seam
cons: Adds a new optional field to ProviderExecResult

options.name: B: surface raw provider stdout and parse it at the dispatch seam
cons: Violates the raw-output-never-surfaced security invariant (raw transcript flows downstream)
Risks credential leakage and transcript promotion into gate evidence
Larger blast radius on a security-sensitive seam

options.name: C: parse usage in the runner and surface a canonical LedgerUsage
cons: Forces providers/ to import usage-ledger (LedgerUsage), breaking the zero-cross-module-import discipline
Couples the provider layer to the ledger schema

chosen: A: runner extracts token-count-only usage; neutral reportedUsage; canonical per-provider final at the seam
rationale: Option A is the only one satisfying all three drivers at once: it surfaces only non-sensitive token-count numbers (security invariant held), keeps providers/ free of usage-ledger imports (neutral Record), and reuses the existing openai/gemini support in buildProviderRecord. Option B violates the security invariant; Option C breaks the import discipline.

preMortem.scenario: Raw provider transcript leaks downstream via reportedUsage
preMortem.trigger: The extractor returns more than the usage object (e.g. the whole parsed envelope including message text)
preMortem.consequence: A provider transcript could be surfaced or promoted into gate evidence, breaking the security invariant
preMortem.mitigation: extractCodex/GeminiUsage returns ONLY the usage/usageMetadata sub-object (token-count keys); the smoke asserts reportedUsage carries only numeric token fields and no transcript text

preMortem.scenario: Claude path or ledger-OFF behavior regresses
preMortem.trigger: Refactoring recordDispatchFinal or the seam touches the shared claude code path
preMortem.consequence: Existing claude usage records change or the OFF path writes a file, breaking byte-identical guarantees
preMortem.mitigation: Add a NEW recordDispatchFinalForProvider and a NEW codex/gemini seam; leave recordDispatchFinal/parseClaudeCliOutput/runClaudeCodeRealLeafDispatch untouched; smoke asserts claude + OFF paths unchanged

preMortem.trigger: Surfacing reportedUsage as LedgerUsage or calling an adapter inside the runner
preMortem.consequence: Breaks the zero-cross-module-import discipline; the import-boundary smoke fails
preMortem.mitigation: reportedUsage is a provider-neutral Record<string,unknown>; adaptation happens only at the dispatch-usage seam; the existing import-boundary static check stays green

preMortem.scenario: A ledger or parse error breaks a real codex/gemini dispatch
preMortem.trigger: Malformed CLI stdout or a writer error in the new seam
preMortem.consequence: Dispatch fails or hangs where it previously succeeded
preMortem.mitigation: Every new ledger call is wrapped in try/catch and proceeds on error (fail-open); recordDispatchFinalForProvider never throws; the extractor never throws and returns undefined on no-usage
